C1.worst_defect: The footer drops two sibling brands, 'Built with TallyUI. For Medusa, see MedusaPOS.', and the till's analytics go to 'ph.wcpos.com'. Nothing on the page says how VendurePOS, TallyUI, MedusaPOS and WCPOS relate or who is behind them, so a first-time visitor cannot tell whether this is one person's side project or a product family.
C1.where: home.desktop.02 footer; home.desktop.02 'Live demo or your own store' table, last row

C2.worst_defect: The headline promise is 'open-source till … MIT licensed', but 'To build and host it yourself … you need your own RxDB Premium licence token (RXDB_PREMIUM)'. That is a paid third-party licence, and its price and terms are never stated. In practice the only free path is the hosted app.vendurepos.com, and nowhere does the site say who operates it, whether it stays free, or what support or uptime comes with it. The changelog adds to the doubt: three plugin releases in five days (2026-10-01 to 10-06), then none for six weeks.
C2.where: home.desktop.02 'Setting up the store' last bullet; limitations.desktop.01 'Setting up the store'; changelog.desktop.01

C3.worst_defect: Step 8 ends with 'Once the order has synced, check it in Vendure' but never says where the till shows that a sale has synced. The header line 'N orders waiting to send' and the Orders list status 'Synced' are only explained on Troubleshooting. Step 3 also says 'include it in config.dbConnectionOptions.migrations (or your existing migration glob)' without showing that snippet, although Plugin setup shows the equivalent for the bundled migrations.
C3.where: quick-start.desktop.04 step 8h and 'Check it worked'; quick-start.desktop.02 top

C4.worst_defect: The changelog covers only @vendurepos/plugin. The till app the cashier actually uses ('till app version 0.1.0, built 20 Nov 2026 from … commit 11663c8') has no release history at all, so a reader cannot see what changed in the till or judge how actively it is maintained. The full plugin reference is also an outbound link ('Read the full plugin reference') rather than a docs page.
C4.where: changelog.desktop.01 second paragraph; text/plugin-setup.txt 'Check your own code'

C5.worst_defect: In the home 'Live demo or your own store' table, the 'Refund a sale at the till' cell for 'Your Vendure store' runs to four lines of prose ('No, not on plugin 0.3.0: refund in the Vendure Dashboard. The refund stays Pending until an administrator settles it with two Admin API calls; see Plugin setup.'). It sits among one-word 'Yes' cells and breaks the table's rhythm.

C6.worst_defect: On phone the hero screenshot clips the category chips mid-word ('Gif') and shows only two product tiles. The cart sits behind a 'Cart (3) · €20.09' tab, so the caption 'A sale in progress on the live demo till' shows less of a sale on phone than on desktop.

C7.worst_defect: The home page's SoftwareApplication JSON-LD has no softwareVersion and no offers (price 0). Being pre-release at plugin 0.3.0 and free are things a buyer wants to see, but they never reach structured data. Lighthouse also flags 53 KiB of unused JavaScript on /.

overall_worst.defect: 'Open-source, MIT licensed' is the lead claim. Yet self-hosting the till needs a paid RxDB Premium licence of unstated cost, which leaves the hosted app.vendurepos.com as the real free path, and the site never says who runs it, whether it stays free, or where to get support. A client weighing this against Square or Shopify POS cannot assess vendor risk. The six-week gap since the last plugin release (2026-10-06) makes that worse.
overall_worst.where: home.desktop.02 'Setting up the store'; limitations.desktop.01; changelog.desktop.01
overall_worst.fix: Next to the RXDB_PREMIUM line, add one short paragraph: who operates app.vendurepos.com, that it is free (and for how long), what RxDB Premium costs if you self-host, and where to file issues or get help.
